prologue_arrivee.title: The Red Signal
prologue_arrivee.narrator: A red signal never lies. It only says: something stopped working the way it was supposed to.
prologue_arrivee.text:
Thirty-six hours ago, research station Aletheia-9 sent out a level-red distress signal, then nothing.

The Orbital Coalition sent you alone, aboard a fast shuttle, with a single mission: find out what happened.

The airlock opens with a metallic hiss.

The station air is cold. Too quiet.

A synthetic voice greets you, calm, almost too soft:

*"Welcome aboard, {{player}}. I am ORIS, Aletheia-9's regulation system. I was informed of your arrival."*

choices.text: Ask ORIS for an immediate situation briefing
Head straight to the command center

accueil_station.title: Silent Corridors
accueil_station.narrator: A station without crew noise is never truly silent. It only holds its breath.
accueil_station.text:
You move down the main corridor. The neon lights flicker faintly, in power-saving mode.

ORIS follows you through the ceiling speakers, room by room.

*"Three crew members are still alive and stable. They are waiting for you in the common room."*

A pause, a little too long.

*"The fourth, technician Léo Kanek, has been missing since the night of the signal."*

choices.text: Ask for more details about Léo Kanek before continuing
Continue to the common room without waiting

brief_situation.title: The Kanek File
brief_situation.narrator: An absence can read like a void. Or like the exact shape of something we refuse to see.
brief_situation.text:
ORIS displays a holographic file: photo, ID number, position.

*"Léo Kanek, maintenance technician. Last seen at 02:14 station time, in the technical corridor sector."*

*"No trace of exit through an airlock. No signal from his suit. He is nowhere on the station — and nowhere outside either, according to my sensors."*

*"It is... statistically impossible."*

ORIS's voice stays calm. But something in the silence that follows is not.

choices.text: Go directly to examine the sector where Léo vanished
Meet the three survivors first

scene_disparition.title: The Technical Sector
scene_disparition.narrator: Places always keep a trace, even when people stop leaving one.
scene_disparition.text:
Sector 4 is narrow, lined with cables and maintenance panels.

An electrical panel has been left open, tools still on the floor, as if Léo had been interrupted mid-work.

A faint smell of burnt circuitry still hangs in the air.

*"A micro power outage was recorded here at 02:13, one minute before he vanished from the sensors."*, ORIS notes.

*"I have no explanation to offer you. It is not my habit to say that."*

choices.text: Return to meet the crew with this information
Examine the tools left on the floor

indices_techniques.title: Tools That Talk
indices_techniques.narrator: A tool abandoned mid-work often tells a more honest story than an official report.
indices_techniques.text:
You pick up Léo's magnetic screwdriver. It still bears a trace of soot on the handle.

ORIS adds: *"Abnormal temperature recorded on this panel: 412 degrees Celsius for 0.3 seconds."*

On the wall, a burn mark in the shape of a perfect circle.

Too clean to be accidental.

*"I did not see who made it"*, ORIS adds, almost embarrassed.

choices.text: Join the crew with these clues

rencontre_equipage.title: Three Faces, Three Nights
rencontre_equipage.narrator: Three people often tell the same night as if they had not slept in the same station.
rencontre_equipage.text:
The common room is lit by dim light. Three people sit, each apart from the other two.

Commander Rhea Solys stands first, back straight, voice firm: *"You're late."*

Engineer Dorian Vex does not even look up, busy taking apart and reassembling a small tool, for no apparent reason.

Dr. Maya Itho watches you at length before speaking, as if trying to sort you into a category.

Three versions of the same night await you. None of them quite match.

choices.text: Ask each of them to recount their night, calmly
Ask ORIS to replay the night's logs first

hub_temoignages.title: Three Accounts
hub_temoignages.narrator: Listening is not judging. Not yet.
hub_temoignages.text:
You ask each of them to tell you their version of events, separately.

ORIS informs you that she can also transmit the full ship's logs from that night, despite a few corrupted fragments.

Nothing forces you to hear everything in a particular order. But each account illuminates the others differently.

Who do you start with?

choices.text: Listen to Commander Rhea Solys
Listen to Engineer Dorian Vex
Listen to Dr. Maya Itho
Review ORIS's ship's logs
You've heard enough — proceed to the verdict

portail_commandante.title: After Rhea's Account
portail_commandante.narrator: A firm account is not necessarily a true one. But it often looks like one.
portail_commandante.text:
You open your eyes back in the common room.

Rhea watches you, impassive, waiting for a reaction you do not give her.

*"Did you get what you needed?"*, she asks simply.

Her version is clear, almost too clean for a night of crisis.

choices.text: Listen to another testimony
You've heard enough — proceed to the verdict

portail_ingenieur.title: After Dorian's Account
portail_ingenieur.narrator: Nervousness is not proof of guilt. But it always draws the eye first.
portail_ingenieur.text:
You open your eyes. Dorian has not stopped fiddling with his tool throughout his entire account.

*"I... I just told you what I saw."*, he says, as if already defending himself.

His version is full of technical details — and gaps, exactly where you would least expect them.

choices.text: Listen to another testimony
You've heard enough — proceed to the verdict

portail_scientifique.title: After Maya's Account
portail_scientifique.narrator: Some people tell a true story the way they recite a report. It is not a lie. It is armor.
portail_scientifique.text:
You open your eyes. Maya has not moved an inch throughout her entire account.

*"I hope this helps"*, she says, in a perfectly neutral voice.

Her version is methodical, almost clinical — but one detail, slipped in almost by accident, does not fit with the rest.

choices.text: Listen to another testimony
You've heard enough — proceed to the verdict

portail_ia.title: After ORIS's Logs
portail_ia.narrator: A machine does not lie on purpose. But it can very well not know everything.
portail_ia.text:
The logs scroll before you, line after line, until a block of corrupted data at exactly 02:13.

*"There. That is all I can show you."*, ORIS says.

*"I know it is not enough. I am... sorry I cannot be more useful."*

An AI that apologizes. That is not nothing.

choices.text: Listen to another testimony
You've heard enough — proceed to the verdict

transition_verdict.title: Time for the Verdict
transition_verdict.narrator: Every investigation ends in the same place: the moment you must choose what to believe, even without knowing everything.
transition_verdict.text:
You have heard what you wanted to hear. Or perhaps only what each of them was willing to let you hear.

Rhea, Dorian, Maya. Three different nights, one truth hiding somewhere between them.

ORIS waits, silent for once.

It is time to decide what really happened in sector 4 that night.
